- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for short-term (1–7d) and 20–40% for long-term (10–30d) horizons.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for short-term, 15–35% for long-term.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., >1.00), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 20–50% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true values when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.67); apply a “mean reversion” bias: add 5–15% to forecast for 10–30d horizon if sentiment is low or flat.
- For 30d forecasts, if model shows high volatility or erratic peaks (e.g., >5x median), apply a “smoothness penalty”: dampen outliers by 30–60% if preceded by high sentiment or low volatility.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +1.00 to -0.33), model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment lag” correction: delay forecast adjustment by 1–3 days and reduce magnitude by 20–40%.
